subject: Urgent: replacement of transit subprocessor and clarification on egress paths
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@edgevault.com>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.com
Cc: legal@edgevault.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Notice: transit subprocessor replaced — questions on cross-border egress

Hi Connor,

Quick heads up from our procurement/compliance team — we received a notice that Redwood intends to replace the transit processor currently routing log and metrics traffic (StreamRelay) with a new provider, EdgeBridge Inc. Our security team flagged two immediate questions we need clarified before we sign off on the change:

1) Egress countries: will the new transit path introduce any new non-EU jurisdictions where customer data (including logs and IP addresses) will transit or be stored temporarily? Please list all countries, even if only transient.

2) Access controls & KMS: will EdgeBridge have any access to encryption keys or plaintext logs? If not, describe the encryption boundary and KMS ownership.

3) Evidence: can you provide the updated subprocessor roster and a brief export map showing ingress/egress hops for EU-region traffic? Our timeline is tight — we need to complete our internal review by COB Thursday Nov 12.

If helpful, you can redact internal hostnames but we need the country-level egress and whether logs traverse any US-based instances.

Thanks,
Maria Gomez
Head of Security & Vendor Risk
EdgeVault

Subject: RE: Notice: transit subprocessor replaced — questions on cross-border egress

Hi Maria — attaching the requested artifacts and a short summary below. Apologies for the quick turnaround, we pushed for details from the infra team.

Summary of change:
- Previous transit vendor: StreamRelay (contract terminated, decommission scheduled).
- New transit vendor: EdgeBridge Inc. — contracted as a pure network transit layer with no persistent storage SLA beyond short-lived buffering (max 60 seconds). EdgeBridge operates relay nodes in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt), eu-west-1 (Ireland), and us-central-1 (Iowa) for redundancy; for EU-region customer traffic we configure routing to prefer eu nodes.

Egress countries (EU customer traffic):
- Primary: Germany (DE), Ireland (IE) — these are the termination/relay nodes for EU traffic.
- Fallback/relay paths: intermittent transient hops may traverse the Netherlands (NL).
- No planned transit or storage in the United States for EU-region production traffic; however, EdgeBridge's control-plane telemetry aggregates anonymized metrics in their US telemetry collector (no PII, no plaintext logs).

KMS and access controls:
- Redwood retains full ownership of encryption keys in our managed KMS (Redwood-managed, HSM-backed). EdgeBridge is only provided with TLS-protected transit endpoints and does not receive KMS credentials or plaintext log access.
- Buffering at EdgeBridge is in-memory only and encrypted in transit. We have contractual clause 7.4 that prohibits EdgeBridge from persisting payloads beyond 60s and from decrypting any payloads.

Evidence & artifacts attached:
- subprocessor_roster_v2.csv (current roster; includes effective dates and contract references)
- egress_map.pdf (diagram showing country hops for eu region)
- dpa_amendment_draft.docx (draft text for the narrow DPA addendum to reflect EdgeBridge as an approved transit-only subprocessor)

Next steps we propose:
1) You review the DPA language in dpa_amendment_draft.docx and flag any required edits.
2) If acceptable, we can route the amendment via DocuSign and aim to have countersigned by both parties by Nov 20.

If your team needs SOC 2-specific subservice mapping for EdgeBridge, we can request a scoped attestation from them but that will add ~1 week to turnaround. Let us know whether that's required for sign-off this week.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Vendor Ops | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v2.csv (CSV), egress_map.pdf (PDF), dpa_amendment_draft.docx (DOCX)

Kimberly/Connor — thanks for the thorough summary and the artifacts. A couple quick clarifications before we kick off legal review:

1) When you say 'no planned transit or storage in the United States for EU-region production traffic', can you confirm the enforcement mechanism? Is routing policy enforced by geography-aware BGP filters or by EdgeBridge config tied to our tenant ID? We need a short statement we can include in our internal memo.

2) Please confirm whether the EdgeBridge control-plane telemetry that lands in the US contains any IP-level data tied to customer flows. If so, we need the scoped attestation you mentioned.

Legal request: our counsel asked that the DPA addendum include a sentence that EdgeBridge will accept jurisdictional obligations for EU data transfers (i.e., comply with SCCs or equivalent safeguards). Can Redwood update the dpa_amendment_draft.docx to include that clause or confirm that EdgeBridge will sign the SCCs?

If you can add the enforcement wording and a quick yes/no on telemetry IPs, we can proceed to a redline request for the DPA and aim to complete sign-off by Nov 20. We'll also queue a DocuSign link on our side if Redwood prefers.

Thanks — Maria
